verdict: Expeditors' freight business boomed on AI-hyperscaler demand: revenue jumped 42% to $4.1B and earnings per share rose 62% to $2.65, with headcount up just 1%.

segments.name: Airfreight services
segments.note: Arranging air cargo for customers — tonnage rose 13% and rates were elevated, on demand from AI hyperscalers and other technology customers.

segments.name: Customs brokerage & other services
segments.note: Clearing goods through customs and related services — work that grows when trade rules get complicated.

segments.name: Ocean freight & ocean services
segments.note: Arranging container shipping by sea — container volumes rose 7%, with rates and demand much stronger than a year ago.

opex.name: Salaries & related costs
opex.note: Pay for about 20,000 logistics staff — headcount rose only 1% while revenue rose 42%, the quarter's operating leverage.

opex.name: Rent & occupancy
opex.note: Offices and facilities around the world.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: A light charge — Expeditors owns few hard assets; it buys transport from carriers instead.

otherDetail: Other income of $3M, net: $6M of interest income, partly offset by $3M of other expense. Net earnings in the flow are rounded; $345M was attributable to shareholders, matching the $2.65 diluted EPS.

takeaways.title: A demand surge, led by AI freight
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 42% to $4.11B. Airfreight revenue jumped 51% and ocean 48%, as AI hyperscalers and other technology customers shipped far more, and as tariff-related customs work grew.

takeaways.title: Headcount barely moved
takeaways.text: Staffing rose just 1% while operating income rose 55% to $445M — operating margin expanded to 10.8% from 10.0%. That leverage is why EPS rose even faster, up 62% to $2.65.

takeaways.title: Cash back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Expeditors returned $197M in the quarter and $946M year to date through dividends and share repurchases, including buying back 1.1 million shares in Q3.

footerNote: Logistics layout: directly related cost of transportation and other expenses ($2,894M — what Expeditors pays airlines, shipping lines and other carriers) is treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining operating lines mirror its condensed consolidated statements of earnings. Figures are rounded to the nearest $M (revenue $4,107.6M in the release). Segment revenues are the service lines reported in the release and Form 10-Q.
